# Gyral error codes

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/errors.mjs` from packages/core/src/view/messages.ts. Do not edit. -->

Development builds of `@gyral/core` print each message in full. Production builds print its
code, its arguments (in the order of the placeholders below) and a link here:
`Gyral G0010 my-cart Increment https://gyral.dev/errors/#G0010`. The table is
[errors.json](errors.json) (gyral-c5d.13), also published with the package as
`@gyral/core/errors.json` (`import errors from '@gyral/core/errors.json' with { type: 'json' }`),
for tools and docs sites that render the codes.

## Components

### G0001

> \<{tag}> is a browser element (render it on the server with @gyral/ssr).

Arguments: `tag`.

### G0010

> \<{tag}> has no update for message "{message}".

Arguments: `tag`, `message`.

### G0011

> \<{tag}> has no intent parser for data-intent="{intent}".

Arguments: `tag`, `intent`.

### G0012

> \<{tag}> intent parser for "{intent}" failed

Arguments: `tag`, `intent`.

### G0013

> \<{tag}> focus("{selector}") matched no focusable element.

Arguments: `tag`, `selector`.

### G0014

> \<{tag}> is on the page, but no custom element named "{tag}" is defined {seconds} s after it loaded, so it renders nothing. If it is one of your components, import the module that calls define()('{tag}', …) from the entry; for a third-party element, load its package. Ignore this for an element defined later on purpose.

Arguments: `tag`, `seconds`.

### G0015

> Two copies of @gyral/core run in this page: {first} from {firstUrl}, and {second} from {secondUrl}. A value one copy makes, such as a stylesheet from css or a store, does not work in the other. Install one copy: pin @gyral/core to one version with your package manager's overrides (gyral() warns when it is installed more than once).

Arguments: `first`, `firstUrl`, `second`, `secondUrl`.

### G0016

> {package} {version} needs @gyral/core {version}, but this app has @gyral/core {core}. Gyral's packages are released together: install the same version of every @gyral package.

Arguments: `package`, `version`, `core`.

### G0017

> \<{tag}> rendered differently with the same state, props and stores, so its view reads something else, such as Date.now(), a module variable or the DOM, or builds a value anew each render that is compared by reference (a Date, a Set, a class instance). It differs {where}. A component renders only when one of them changes (0.3.8): move what the view reads into state, a prop or a store.

Arguments: `tag`, `where`.

### G0018

> The parser of intent "{intent}" is on("{expected}"), but a "{actual}" event reached it. Bind the intent to that event (data-intent-{expected}=${…}), or give it a parser of its own.

Arguments: `intent`, `expected`, `actual`.

## Props

### G0020

> \<{tag}> prop "{prop}" has an asynchronous schema; it must be synchronous.

Arguments: `tag`, `prop`.

### G0021

> \<{tag}> prop "{prop}" got an invalid value from {source}, so it is treated as missing: {issues}

Arguments: `tag`, `prop`, `source`, `issues`.

### G0022

> \<{tag}> is missing required prop(s): {props}.

Arguments: `tag`, `props`.

### G0023

> \<{tag}> declares prop(s) named like a member every element already has: {props}. The prop would replace it: a prop named "hidden" hides the element, one named "state" hides the component's model. Rename the property. The name of one of Gyral's members (state, send, drivers, stores) can stay the attribute: badge: prop.string({ attribute: "state" }).

Arguments: `tag`, `props`.

### G0024

> \<{tag}> has a "{attribute}" attribute, which no prop reads: HTML lowercases attribute names, and prop {prop} reads "{expected}". Write {expected}="…", or set the property (el.{prop} = …).

Arguments: `tag`, `attribute`, `prop`, `expected`.

## Scheduling

### G0030

> gyral: a deferred callback failed

Arguments: none.

### G0031

> \<{tag}> view failed; it shows its error view, or its previous DOM stays.

Arguments: `tag`.

### G0032

> gyral: post-render work failed

Arguments: none.

### G0033

> gyral: rendering did not settle in one flush (a cycle between {tags}). Components are probably feeding each other props or messages; break the cycle with a condition in update.

Arguments: `tags`.

### G0034

> settled(): the page did not settle after {rounds} flushes or busy turns. A stream is emitting without pause, or components (or drivers) are feeding each other messages in a cycle.

Arguments: `rounds`.

## Commands

### G0040

> {owner}: the onSuccess or onFailure mapper for driver "{driver}" threw; no message was sent.

Arguments: `owner`, `driver`.

### G0041

> {owner}: driver "{driver}" failed and the command has no onFailure.

Arguments: `owner`, `driver`.

### G0042

> gyral: subscription "{name}" failed to unsubscribe

Arguments: `name`.

### G0043

> {owner}: no driver provides "{driver}". It is a driver token: provide its implementation with provideDrivers(root, [token.provide(run)]) or el.drivers. A page provides it before its components' first render: before importing them, or later in the same task (no await in between).

Arguments: `owner`, `driver`.

### G0044

> Two drivers named "{name}" in one list of drivers: give each a name of its own, or drop one.

Arguments: `name`.

### G0045

> A driver supplied as "{key}" is named "{name}", so commands of the "{name}" driver never use it. Supply drivers as a list, each under its own name (provideDrivers(root, [driver])), or make the key match.

Arguments: `key`, `name`.

## Stores

### G0050

> \<{tag}> uses store "{store}" without declaring it. Add it to the spec: stores: [{store}], so the component subscribes to its changes.

Arguments: `tag`, `store`.

### G0051

> store "{store}": the server's seed failed its schema, so it starts from init. Issues: {issues}

Arguments: `store`, `issues`.

### G0052

> unreadable {attribute} seed on {where}

Arguments: `attribute`, `where`.

### G0053

> \<{tag}> reads store "{store}" during a server render without a store scope. Pass the request's store instances to renderPage({ stores }) or renderToString(value, { stores }).

Arguments: `tag`, `store`.

### G0054

> store "{store}" sends to "{target}" but is not held by a store scope (a registry, \<gyral-stores> or the page default), so the message is dropped.

Arguments: `store`, `target`.

### G0055

> store "{store}" has no update for message "{message}".

Arguments: `store`, `message`.

## Hydration

### G0060

> \<{tag}> has an unreadable {attribute}

Arguments: `tag`, `attribute`.

### G0061

> gyral: hydration code failed to load; rendering fresh

Arguments: none.

### G0062

> gyral: hydration mismatch in {host} at {path}: expected {expected}, found {found}. The server's HTML differs from the first client render: a view that isn't deterministic (Date.now(), locale), a third party that changed the DOM before scripts ran, or a stale cached page (https://gyral.dev/docs/server-rendering/#mismatches).

Arguments: `host`, `path`, `expected`, `found`.

### G0063

> \<{tag}> was rendered fresh after a hydration mismatch:

Arguments: `tag`.

## Templates

### G0069

> \<{element}> ?{binding} does nothing: this build left the dialog and popover code out, because no module the build scanned binds it (a package that does not depend on Gyral is not scanned).

Arguments: `element`, `binding`.

### G0070

> gyral: an html template was not compiled: `{start}`. Under the gyral-compiled condition every html`…` must be compiled by the Gyral Vite preset.

Arguments: `start`.

### G0071

> gyral: template rule 11: a page shell rendered in the browser.

Arguments: none.

### G0072

> gyral: this page's Trusted Types policy list does not allow the policy "gyral", so templates are parsed from plain strings, which works only while Trusted Types are not enforced. Add `trusted-types gyral` to the Content-Security-Policy.

Arguments: none.

### G0073

> \<{tag}> update for "{message}" failed; the state is unchanged.

Arguments: `tag`, `message`.

### G0074

> \<{tag}> init failed; it shows its error view, or stays empty.

Arguments: `tag`.

### G0075

### G0076

> store "{store}": update for "{message}" failed; the state is unchanged.

## Subscriptions

### G0079

> \<{tag}> subscriptions returned two commands for lane "{lane}"; only the first runs. Give each its own `key`.

Arguments: `tag`, `lane`.

### G0080

> \<{tag}> subscriptions kept restarting: a subscription's input data changes with every message it sends (for example a timestamp or a counter in the input). Keep inputs to what should restart it; functions are ignored, so to restart on a new selector, change the key.

Arguments: `tag`.
